learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knows the fundamentals of thermal machines and engines and different energy transformation technologies.
Understands the analysis of work production cycles, integrating the operation of the main equipment.
Has the capacity and criteria to analyze, size, select, and design equipment for the utilization, production, and transformation of mechanical energy.
Is capable of applying thermal engines in combined energy production systems for industry.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to thermal machines and engines.
Ideal and real cycles of internal combustion reciprocating engines (ICRE).
ICRE subsystems and components. Operating and design parameters.
Compressible flow. Nozzles and diffusers. Propulsion. Fundamentals of thermal turbomachinery. Euler equation. Velocity triangle.
Degree of reaction and types of turbine stages. Losses.
Compressors: types, characteristics, and selection criteria.
Application of thermal machines and engines to electricity generation.
Selection criteria and optimization of thermal machine and engine operation in energy production systems.
Descriptive analysis of ICREs and thermal turbomachines.
Determination of the dragging capacity of a vehicle's ICRE.
Basic design of an axial reaction gas turbine.
Resolution of practical cases for ICREs and thermal turbomachines. Rankine cycle.
Optimal sizing of a simple cogeneration system.
teaching_methods: In-person class (Expository sessions of theoretical and applied content, presentation of basic concepts and fundamentals).
Problem-solving classes (Problems and cases developed, students encouraged to work on problems beforehand, with statements and resolution guidelines provided).

Laboratory practicals (Five sessions covering descriptive analysis of machines/engines, design/analysis of positive displacement machines, design/analysis of thermal turbomachines, practical cases, analysis/optimization of power/cogeneration plants).
Assignments (Individual or group activities proposed by the professor, with tutoring sessions for follow-up).
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, written tests account for 80% and practicals for 20%. To pass, a minimum of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in each written test and in the practicals combined, with an overall grade of 5 out of 10 or higher. Students not opting for or not passing continuous assessment, or those in the second call, will be evaluated via a single global written exam covering all course content.
